title: Portability: commit the import event plan through a durable store port
description:
Filed by architect-c9e91335 while planning task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8, under the global rail requiring prerequisite production tasks when a claimed capability is measured absent. This is a PRODUCER gap, measured symbol by symbol at HEAD 8222b9e2.

MEASURED GAP. `applyImport` (packages/import/src/import-apply.ts:196) ends by calling `input.store.commit({ aggregateId: `legacy-import:${manifest.digest}`, commandBytes, commandId, committedAt, events, expectedVersion: 0 })` at :219-228, wrapping failure as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY. So the commit PLAN is production-complete: aggregate id, command identity, committedAt and the `ImportEventDraft[]` (each now carrying `domainSchemaVersion: IMPORT_EVENT_FACTS_VERSION` since task-9745cd06b8004f44af4128f69a251860 landed at import-apply.ts:43,162).

WHAT IS ABSENT is anything that binds that port to a real store:
- `grep -rn "applyImport" apps tools packages --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns exactly TWO non-test composers: packages/import/src/index.ts:19 (the re-export) and tools/import/import-shadow.ts:141.
- That single composer passes DISCARDING_STORE, defined at tools/import/import-shadow.ts:111 as `commit: () => ({ currentVersion: 0 })`, and the file's own header states "the comparator never sees an authority-bearing store" — by rail, not by accident.
- `grep -rn "@moe/import" apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns ZERO. The daemon does not reference the importer at all.

CONSEQUENCE. No production path has ever written a `legacy.<kind>.imported` event to a SqliteEventStore. The `legacy-import:<manifestDigest>` aggregate is empty in every real deployment, so any durable reader over it correctly answers ABSENT forever, and a shadow comparison against it is vacuous rather than wrong.

DELIVERABLE. One focused production adapter that implements the `ImportStorePort` `commit` shape over a real SqliteEventStore and is invoked on a real import path, so the drafted events become durable rows with their stamped `domainSchemaVersion`. It writes only what `applyImport` drafted — it derives no facts, re-encodes no payload, and adds no event.

NOT IN SCOPE: the durable reader/mapper (task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8 owns it), the shadow matrix (task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93), activation, cutover, or any dual write. The read-only posture of tools/import/import-shadow.ts is deliberate and must not be changed to satisfy this task — if the durable write belongs behind a daemon command rather than that CLI, say so and place it there.

CONSUMER: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 needs this to have non-vacuous current-side rows; task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8's reader is independently correct without it and is NOT blocked by this task.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "applyImport" apps packages --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` names a production composer that passes a store port backed by a real SqliteEventStore, where today the only non-test composer passes tools/import/import-shadow.ts:111's DISCARDING_STORE.

The adapter commits exactly the `ImportEventDraft[]` that `applyImport` drafted, at the aggregate id and command identity `applyImport` derived, with `expectedVersion: 0`; a test asserts the durable rows' `domainSchemaVersion` equals IMPORT_EVENT_FACTS_VERSION and that the stored payload bytes are byte-identical to the drafted bytes.
The adapter derives no fact, re-encodes no payload and adds no event: a mutation that re-encodes a payload before committing, or appends one extra event, turns a NAMED test red.

A second commit of the same manifest digest conflicts rather than appending a duplicate aggregate, and the refusal keeps its own exact code and layer rather than being restamped as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED; raw event and decision counts prove the original survives.

Real SqliteEventStore tests read the committed rows back through public `decodeImportEventFacts` and assert a nonzero decoded claim count; a store failure surfaces as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY from `applyImport` itself, asserted by exact code and layer.
Package typecheck and test run with exit codes captured separately and a nonzero `Test Files N passed` count line; only owned paths are committed.
taskRails: Dependency direction is consumer -> @moe/import through public roots only. Never add a dependency from @moe/import toward apps/daemon or @moe/store.
Commit only what applyImport drafted. This adapter is a port implementation, not a producer: no fact derivation, no re-encoding, no extra event, no dual write, no activation, no cutover.

Do not change the read-only posture of tools/import/import-shadow.ts. Its DISCARDING_STORE and 'the comparator never sees an authority-bearing store' header are deliberate; if the durable write belongs behind a daemon command, place it there instead.
Preserve upstream IMPORT_* code and layer verbatim rather than restamping; a store-level conflict is not IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED.
Use TDD with a real SqliteEventStore, assert exact codes and layers, target <=250 physical lines per production source, and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Confirm the measurement and settle PLACEMENT, the one genuinely open decision. Read-only. Re-verify at committed HEAD: (a) `applyImport` (packages/import/src/import-apply.ts:196) commits through `ImportStorePort` at :219-228 with `expectedVersion: 0`, wrapping only THROWN failures as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY; (b) the only non-test composer is tools/import/import-shadow.ts:141 passing DISCARDING_STORE (:111), whose file header asserts read-only ON BYTES (pre/post digest of every manifest-covered file) -- that posture is rail-protected and must not change; (c) `grep -rn "@moe/import" apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns ZERO. THE SHAPE LUCK THAT MAKES THIS ADAPTER THIN, verify each: `ImportCommitInput` {aggregateId, commandBytes, commandId, committedAt, events, expectedVersion} is field-for-field a subset-compatible shape of the store's `CommitInput` (store-contracts.ts:46-53); `ImportEventDraft` {domainSchemaVersion, eventId, eventType, payload} maps onto the store's `EventDraft` whose `domainSchemaVersion` is OPTIONAL with a generic default (:36-44) -- which is precisely why the import draft made it REQUIRED (import-apply.ts:39-42's own comment: an omitted field persists an envelope schema the stored bytes do not speak). PLACEMENT DECISION, recorded here per the task rail's invitation: the adapter and its CLI entry live in `tools/import/` as a NEW file beside import-shadow.ts -- NOT inside packages/import (the rail forbids @moe/import depending on @moe/store), NOT inside apps/daemon (zero @moe/import references exist there today, and inventing a daemon command kind for import would widen the frozen command vocabulary, a far larger change this task must not smuggle), and NOT inside import-shadow.ts (read-only by rail). tools/ is not a workspace package, so imports are deep relative specifiers with the file named in a root typecheck script -- import-shadow.ts's own header documents this exact precedent and why it does not trip TS6059.

RED. Create tools/import/import-commit.test.ts (or the location's existing test convention if tools/ tests live elsewhere -- check for one first; if tools/ has NO test convention, put the suite at tests/integration and note why). Tests against a REAL SqliteEventStore on a temp file, driving the REAL `applyImport` with a small fixture manifest and records -- never a hand-built ImportCommitInput, because the DoD's byte-identity claim is about what applyImport DRAFTED. Failing tests: (1) HAPPY PATH: after applyImport succeeds through the adapter, read the `legacy-import:<manifestDigest>` aggregate back and assert a nonzero event count, each row's `domainSchemaVersion` === IMPORT_EVENT_FACTS_VERSION (the literal, imported from the package), and each stored payload byte-identical to the drafted payload; decode the rows through public `decodeImportEventFacts` and assert a NONZERO decoded claim count -- a zero-claim decode passes vacuously and DoD 5 names this. (2) DUPLICATE MANIFEST: a second applyImport over the same manifest digest must CONFLICT, not append -- assert the refusal carries the STORE'S own conflict code and layer, NOT restamped as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED, and assert raw event and decision counts prove the original aggregate survived unchanged. Note the subtlety: applyImport catches THROWN commit failures as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED/APPLY, so the adapter must let a version-conflict answer flow through as a RETURN or a typed refusal rather than throwing it -- decide the mechanism from the store's actual conflict behaviour (measure whether SqliteEventStore.commit throws or returns on expectedVersion mismatch) and pin WHICH layer answers in the test. (3) STORE FAILURE: a genuinely broken store (closed handle) surfaces as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY from applyImport itself -- assert exact code and layer.

GREEN. Create tools/import/import-commit.ts: the durable `ImportStorePort` implementation plus a minimal CLI entry. The port maps ImportCommitInput -> the store's CommitInput field-for-field: same aggregateId, same commandBytes, same commandId, same committedAt, same expectedVersion, and each ImportEventDraft passed through with its REQUIRED domainSchemaVersion preserved -- no spread-with-defaults that could let the store's generic version leak in, no re-encoding of any payload (pass the Uint8Array through untouched), no derived fact, no added event. THE WHOLE ADAPTER IS THE ABSENCE OF TRANSFORMATION, and the DoD's mutation drills exist to prove that absence. Handle the conflict path per the step-2 measurement: surface the store's own conflict code/layer distinctly from a thrown infrastructure failure. The CLI entry composes buildSourceManifest -> decodeLegacySources -> applyImport with THIS port over a real store path given by flag, prints one JSON report, and refuses to run against a store path that does not exist (fail closed; never create a store implicitly). Add the file to the root `typecheck:import` script alongside import-shadow.ts and shadow-input.ts -- that script enumerates files explicitly, so a new file NOT added is silently untypechecked, the exact class the integration-tests-typechecked-by-nothing gotcha records. Keep the production file <=250 physical lines.

Mutation drills, the two DoD 3 names plus the vacuity guard. Drill 1 (no re-encoding): make the adapter re-encode one payload (decode + re-serialise) before committing; the step-2 byte-identity test must go RED on the byte comparison, not on a crash. Drill 2 (no extra event): make the adapter append one synthetic event to the drafted list; a NAMED test must go RED on the exact event count and the decoded claim count. Drill 3 (the decode assertion is real): empty the fixture so applyImport drafts zero claim events; the step-2 happy-path test must go RED on its nonzero-decoded-claims assertion -- if it stays green, the assertion is not actually gating on decoded content and must be strengthened. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in the shared worktree), confirm `git diff --numstat` shows 0 added 0 deleted per drilled file, one drill at a time.

Adversarial review, commit, gate. ATTACKER PASS: can any payload byte differ between draft and row -- including via a defensive copy that normalises, a TextEncoder round-trip, or `.slice()` consulting Symbol.species on hostile input? Does the adapter ever supply a default domainSchemaVersion? Can the CLI write anywhere except the explicitly-flagged store path? Did import-shadow.ts change AT ALL (it must not -- diff it against HEAD to prove zero bytes moved)? Is the conflict path distinguishable from infrastructure failure by code AND layer, and does neither get restamped? Is the new file in the typecheck:import script? DEPENDENCY-DIRECTION CHECK per the rail: packages/import must gain NO import of @moe/store -- grep it. COMMIT: `git status --porcelain`, unstage foreign entries, commit ONLY tools/import/import-commit.ts, its test file, and the package.json script line by explicit pathspec; verify with `git show --stat`. GATE, per DoD 6 with exit codes captured SEPARATELY (never `;`-chained, never piped): `pnpm typecheck:import` then `pnpm typecheck` then the test command for wherever the suite landed -- each must print its own nonzero `Test Files N passed` count line where applicable; a leg with no count line ran nothing. In the completion note name task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 as the consumer this de-vacuates and state that task-80fce1d1's reader is independently correct and was never blocked by this task, exactly as the description records.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: PLACEMENT was the one real decision; the adapter itself is deliberately trivial. Chose tools/import/import-commit.ts as a sibling of import-shadow.ts. REJECTED: (a) inside packages/import -- the task rail forbids @moe/import depending on @moe/store, and the port abstraction exists precisely so the package never sees a concrete store; (b) inside apps/daemon behind a command -- zero @moe/import references exist in the daemon today, the command vocabulary is frozen with a full-coverage ratchet, and inventing `import.commit` as a kind is a far larger authority decision than this producer-gap task may smuggle; the task rail explicitly says 'if the durable write belongs behind a daemon command, place it there' -- I considered it and the answer is not yet: cutover/activation tasks own that decision, and this task only needs the drafted events to become durable rows on a REAL import path, which a CLI entry satisfies; (c) modifying import-shadow.ts to take a --write flag -- its read-only posture is asserted on BYTES in its own header and rail-protected; a write mode would invalidate its central guarantee. The adapter maps ImportCommitInput to the store's CommitInput field-for-field -- the shapes are already compatible (measured, not assumed), and ImportEventDraft's REQUIRED domainSchemaVersion exists precisely because the store's EventDraft defaults it; the adapter must pass it through explicitly, never spread-with-defaults. The conflict-path subtlety drove test design: applyImport wraps THROWN commit failures as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED/APPLY, so if SqliteEventStore.commit throws on version conflict the adapter must catch and surface the store's code as a typed answer rather than letting it be restamped -- DoD 4 demands the store's own code and layer survive verbatim.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at committed HEAD (8222b9e lineage). PORT: ImportStorePort {commit(ImportCommitInput): ImportCommitOutcome} at packages/import/src/import-apply.ts:63-65; ImportCommitInput {aggregateId, commandBytes, commandId, committedAt, events, expectedVersion} (:49-57); ImportEventDraft {domainSchemaVersion: typeof IMPORT_EVENT_FACTS_VERSION (REQUIRED -- its comment at :39-42 explains an omitted field would persist an envelope schema the stored bytes do not speak), eventId, eventType, payload: Uint8Array} (:38-47). CALL: applyImport commits at :219-228 with expectedVersion: 0 and aggregateId `legacy-import:${manifest.digest}`; only a THROW is wrapped as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY (:229-231). STORE SIDE: SqliteEventStore.commit(input: CommitInput): CommitResult at packages/store/src/sqlite-event-store.ts:257; CommitInput (store-contracts.ts:46-53) is field-compatible; EventDraft (:36-44) has OPTIONAL domainSchemaVersion defaulting to DOMAIN_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION -- the mismatch the import draft guards against. Worker must MEASURE whether commit throws or returns on expectedVersion conflict before writing the conflict test. COMPOSERS: exactly two non-test applyImport references -- packages/import/src/index.ts:19 (re-export) and tools/import/import-shadow.ts:141 with DISCARDING_STORE at :111. import-shadow.ts's header documents: read-only asserted on BYTES (pre/post digests), applyImport composed only to derive claims/links, the comparator never sees an authority-bearing store, AND the tools/ composition precedent -- deep relative specifiers because pnpm-workspace.yaml globs only apps/*, adapters/*, packages/*, with the file named explicitly in root `typecheck:import` (package.json:28), which is why TS6059 does not fire. A new tools/import file MUST be added to that script or it is typechecked by NOTHING (the known integration-tests gotcha class). decodeImportEventFacts is public on the @moe/import root for the read-back assertion.
planningNotes.risks: The defining risk is an adapter that quietly transforms: a defensive copy that re-encodes a payload, a spread that lets the store default domainSchemaVersion, or an added bookkeeping event would all commit successfully and read back plausibly -- only byte-identity and exact-count assertions catch them, which is why DoD 3's two mutations are drills 1 and 2 and why the decode assertion has its own vacuity drill (a sweep decoding zero claims passes while proving nothing, DoD 5's explicit worry). Second, restamping: a version conflict surfacing as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED erases the distinction DoD 4 requires -- the adapter must let the store's own conflict code/layer survive, and the test must pin WHICH layer answered, since applyImport's catch-all sits one frame above. Third, the read-only posture of import-shadow.ts is a guarantee asserted on bytes -- change nothing there, and prove zero-byte diff at review. Fourth, tools/ files are typechecked ONLY via explicit enumeration in the typecheck:import script; forgetting to add the new file leaves it typechecked by nothing and green forever. Fifth, dependency direction: packages/import must gain no @moe/store import -- the whole port design exists to keep that edge out. Sixth, the CLI must fail closed on a missing store path rather than creating one -- an implicitly-created empty store would make the duplicate-manifest test meaningless and could silently write authority rows in a wrong directory. Finally, close every store handle on every path; a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker.
